intro: Hi! Today you learn to talk about the future: your plans (I'm going to save money), predictions from what you can see (Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.) and fixed arrangements with other people (I'm meeting Sari at 5). Warm-up: what's your plan for this weekend?
teachingNotes: Form: am/is/are + going to + plain verb (I'm going to cook, she's going to buy). Indonesian 'saya akan / mau' has no 'be', so the #1 error is dropping it: *'I going to visit my grandma' → 'I'm going to visit my grandma'. The #2 error is adding -s or -ing after 'to': *'She is going to buys a car' → 'She is going to buy a car'. After 'to' the verb never changes.

Explain that 'going to' + verb does not mean 'pergi' here: it's a fixed chunk like 'akan / mau / rencananya'. Contrast: 'I'm going to Bali on Friday' (going to + a place = pergi ke, present continuous of go) vs 'I'm going to swim' (going to + a verb = a plan). Before words that aren't verbs (late, hot, tired, a doctor) add be: 'It's going to be hot', not *'It's going to hot'. 'Gonna' is how fast speech sounds; learners should write 'going to'.

Predictions with going to need evidence you can see or know now: 'Look at the clouds! It's going to rain.' / 'Watch out! You're going to fall.' In 'It's going to rain', 'it' means nothing: English just needs a word at the start (as in 'It's raining').

Fixed arrangements: present continuous + a future time word, for things fixed with other people (a time and often a place, tickets, appointments): 'I'm meeting Sari at the cafe at 5.' Without a time word it means now. Indonesian 'Besok saya ketemu Sari jam 5' leads to *'Tomorrow I meet Sari at 5'; the simple present is for habits, so correct it to 'I'm meeting'.

Plan vs arrangement: keep it simple. Often both are fine ('I'm going to meet Sari on Friday' is not wrong). The present continuous is most natural when the thing is in your calendar with another person; going to is for your own plan or intention. Never mark going to wrong for an arrangement; only push the present continuous when the learner uses the simple present.

Limits: this lesson is the learner's first future lesson. Don't teach will, shall, the present simple for timetables (the train leaves at 6), the past simple or the present perfect. If a learner asks about will, say it comes in the next lesson. Negatives and questions work like 'to be': I'm not going to…, Are you going to…? — Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.

keyPoints.title: Plans: am / is / are + going to + verb
keyPoints.explanation: Use going to for a plan you have now for later (tonight, tomorrow, next week). Form: am/is/are + going to + the plain verb. Never drop am/is/are (Indonesian 'akan' has no 'be'), and never add -s or -ing after 'to'. Negative: I'm not going to… Question: Are you going to…?

examples.id: Bulan depan Rina mau mengunjungi orang tuanya di Surabaya.

id.title: Rencana: am / is / are + going to + kata kerja
id.explanation: Pakai going to untuk rencana yang sudah ada di kepalamu sekarang untuk nanti (nanti malam, besok, minggu depan). Bentuknya: am/is/are + going to + kata kerja bentuk dasar. Jangan pernah hilangkan am/is/are (kata 'akan' dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak punya 'be'), dan jangan tambahkan -s atau -ing setelah 'to'. Negatif: I'm not going to… Pertanyaan: Are you going to…?

keyPoints.title: Predictions from what you can see
keyPoints.explanation: Use going to for a prediction (a guess about the future) when you can see the reason now: dark clouds, a very full glass, heavy traffic. Before words that aren't verbs (late, hot, tired) add be: going to be late.

id.title: Prediksi dari apa yang kamu lihat
id.explanation: Pakai going to untuk prediksi (tebakan tentang masa depan) kalau kamu bisa melihat alasannya sekarang: awan gelap, gelas yang terlalu penuh, jalan yang macet. Sebelum kata yang bukan kata kerja (late, hot, tired), tambahkan be: going to be late.

keyPoints.title: Fixed arrangements: present continuous + a time
keyPoints.explanation: When something is fixed with another person (a time, often a place, a ticket or an appointment), use the present continuous (am/is/are + verb-ing) with a future time word: I'm meeting Sari on Friday. Not the simple present (Tomorrow I meet…): that's for habits.

id.title: Janji yang sudah terjadwal: present continuous + waktu
id.explanation: Kalau sesuatu sudah dijadwalkan dengan orang lain (jamnya, sering juga tempatnya, ada tiket atau janji temu), pakai present continuous (am/is/are + kata kerja-ing) dengan kata waktu masa depan: I'm meeting Sari on Friday. Jangan pakai simple present (Tomorrow I meet…): itu untuk kebiasaan.

blocks.text:
A **plan** is something you have in your head now for later: tonight, tomorrow, next week, next year. To talk about it, say **am / is / are + going to + verb** (the action word): *I'm going to cook. She's going to buy a car.*

Two things to remember:
- **Always use am / is / are.** Indonesian says *saya akan / saya mau* with no extra word, but English needs **be**: *I'm going to visit my grandma*, not `I going to visit`.
- **After to, the verb never changes:** no -s, no -ing, even with he, she or it. *She is going to* **buy**, not `going to buys`.

id.text:
**Rencana** adalah sesuatu yang sudah ada di kepalamu sekarang untuk nanti: nanti malam, besok, minggu depan, tahun depan. Untuk membicarakannya, pakai **am / is / are + going to + kata kerja** (kata kegiatan): *I'm going to cook. She's going to buy a car.*

Dua hal yang perlu diingat:
- **Selalu pakai am / is / are.** Bahasa Indonesia cukup bilang *saya akan / saya mau* tanpa kata tambahan, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh **be**: *I'm going to visit my grandma*, bukan `I going to visit`.
- **Setelah to, kata kerjanya tidak pernah berubah:** tanpa -s, tanpa -ing, walaupun subjeknya he, she atau it. *She is going to* **buy**, bukan `going to buys`.

blocks.text:
**Going to doesn't mean 'pergi' here.** In *I'm going to cook*, *going to* is one fixed piece that means *akan / mau / rencananya*. Look at the word after **to**:
- a **verb** (cook, buy, study) → it's a plan: *I'm going to swim* = saya mau berenang.
- a **place** → it's the normal verb *go* (pergi): *I'm going to the market* = saya (sedang / mau) pergi ke pasar.
In fast speech, *going to* often sounds like **'gonna'**. That's fine to understand, but write *going to*.

id.text:
**Going to di sini bukan berarti 'pergi'.** Dalam *I'm going to cook*, *going to* adalah satu potongan tetap yang artinya *akan / mau / rencananya*. Lihat kata setelah **to**:
- **kata kerja** (cook, buy, study) → itu rencana: *I'm going to swim* = saya mau berenang.
- **tempat** → itu kata kerja *go* biasa (pergi): *I'm going to the market* = saya (sedang / mau) pergi ke pasar.
Kalau orang bicara cepat, *going to* sering terdengar seperti **'gonna'**. Tidak apa-apa untuk dipahami, tapi tulislah *going to*.

blocks.prompt: Complete: My parents ___ visit us next week.
blocks.explain: My parents = they, so use are: are going to visit. 'going to' alone has no be, and 'is' is for one person.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: My parents ___ visit us next week.
id.explain: My parents = they, jadi pakai are: are going to visit. 'going to' saja tidak punya be, dan 'is' untuk satu orang.

blocks.text:
**Negative** (not): put **not** after am / is / are: *I'm not going to work tomorrow. Dimas isn't going to come.* (isn't = is not)

**Question:** put **am / is / are first**: *Are you going to cook tonight?* Short answers: *Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.*

The most useful question: **What are you going to do?** = *Kamu mau ngapain?* Here the first word *do* is the plain verb after *to* (melakukan).

id.text:
**Negatif** (tidak): taruh **not** setelah am / is / are: *I'm not going to work tomorrow. Dimas isn't going to come.* (isn't = is not)

**Pertanyaan:** taruh **am / is / are di depan**: *Are you going to cook tonight?* Jawaban singkat: *Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.*

Pertanyaan yang paling berguna: **What are you going to do?** = *Kamu mau ngapain?* Di sini *do* adalah kata kerja bentuk dasar setelah *to* (melakukan).

material.title: I can see it: It's going to rain

blocks.text:
Going to is also for a **prediction** (a guess about the future) when you can **see the reason now**: *Look at those dark clouds!* **It's going to rain.** You see the clouds, so you know what's coming.

Why *it*? In *It's going to rain*, **it** means nothing: English just needs a word at the start, like in *It's raining*.

With words that aren't verbs, like **late, hot, tired, a big day**, add **be** after going to: *He's going to* **be** *late.* Indonesian says *dia akan terlambat* without a *be*, so learners often write `going to late`.

id.text:
Going to juga dipakai untuk **prediksi** (tebakan tentang masa depan) kalau kamu **bisa melihat alasannya sekarang**: *Look at those dark clouds!* **It's going to rain.** Kamu melihat awannya, jadi kamu tahu apa yang akan terjadi.

Kenapa *it*? Dalam *It's going to rain*, **it** tidak ada artinya: bahasa Inggris hanya butuh kata di awal kalimat, seperti di *It's raining*.

Untuk kata yang bukan kata kerja, seperti **late, hot, tired, a big day**, tambahkan **be** setelah going to: *He's going to* **be** *late.* Bahasa Indonesia bilang *dia akan terlambat* tanpa *be*, jadi banyak yang menulis `going to late`.

material.title: Fixed with someone: I'm meeting Sari at 5

blocks.text:
Some plans are **fixed with another person**: the time (and often the place) is set, you have a ticket or an appointment. It's in your calendar. For these, English often uses the **present continuous** you already know (**am / is / are + verb-ing**) with a **future time word**: *I'm meeting Sari at the cafe at 5.*

The time word is important: *I'm meeting Sari* alone can mean *right now*; *I'm meeting Sari* **on Friday** is clearly the future.

**The Indonesian trap:** *Besok saya ketemu Sari jam 5* doesn't change the verb *ketemu*, so learners say `Tomorrow I meet Sari at 5`. The simple present (*I meet*) is for habits. Say **Tomorrow I'm meeting Sari at 5.**

id.text:
Ada rencana yang **sudah dijadwalkan dengan orang lain**: jamnya (sering juga tempatnya) sudah ditentukan, kamu sudah punya tiket atau janji temu. Sudah masuk kalendermu. Untuk ini, bahasa Inggris sering memakai **present continuous** yang sudah kamu kenal (**am / is / are + kata kerja-ing**) dengan **kata waktu masa depan**: *I'm meeting Sari at the cafe at 5.*

Kata waktunya penting: *I'm meeting Sari* saja bisa berarti *sekarang*; *I'm meeting Sari* **on Friday** jelas masa depan.

**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Besok saya ketemu Sari jam 5* tidak mengubah kata kerjanya, jadi banyak yang bilang `Tomorrow I meet Sari at 5`. Simple present (*I meet*) untuk kebiasaan. Bilang **Tomorrow I'm meeting Sari at 5.**

rows.en: I'm meeting Sari at the cafe at 5.

blocks.text:
**Plan or arrangement?** Often both are fine: *I'm going to meet Sari on Friday* is not wrong. A simple guide:
- It's **in your calendar with another person** (time fixed, ticket, appointment) → **I'm meeting / I'm flying / I'm having dinner…**
- It's **your own idea or plan**, nothing fixed with anyone → **I'm going to…**: *I'm going to clean my room this weekend.*
The one thing that is wrong: the simple present (`Tomorrow I meet Sari`).

id.text:
**Rencana atau janji terjadwal?** Sering keduanya benar: *I'm going to meet Sari on Friday* tidak salah. Panduan sederhananya:
- Sudah **masuk kalender bersama orang lain** (jam sudah ditentukan, ada tiket, ada janji temu) → **I'm meeting / I'm flying / I'm having dinner…**
- Masih **ide atau rencanamu sendiri**, belum dijadwalkan dengan siapa pun → **I'm going to…**: *I'm going to clean my room this weekend.*
Yang pasti salah: simple present (`Tomorrow I meet Sari`).

blocks.prompt: Sari has a meeting with Bu Ani at the bank tomorrow at 9. Complete: Sari ___ Bu Ani at the bank tomorrow at 9.
blocks.explain: It's fixed with another person and has a future time (tomorrow at 9), so use the present continuous: is meeting. 'meets' is for habits, and 'meeting' alone has no is.

id.prompt: Sari ada janji dengan Bu Ani di bank besok jam 9. Lengkapi: Sari ___ Bu Ani at the bank tomorrow at 9.
id.explain: Sudah dijadwalkan dengan orang lain dan ada waktu masa depan (tomorrow at 9), jadi pakai present continuous: is meeting. 'meets' untuk kebiasaan, dan 'meeting' saja tidak punya is.
